items.description: A 7.2 g Wabar impact fragment showing black glass fused directly to pale desert sand, with a jagged boundary between the glassy melt and granular substrate. This is related impact material, not a meteorite.
items.imageAlt: Exact 7.2 g Wabar impact glass and fused sand specimen offered for sale
items.name: Wabar Impact Glass with Fused Sand

items.description: This 4.97 g fragment is from Aguas Zarcas, an officially recognized CM2 carbonaceous chondrite that fell in Alajuela, Costa Rica, on April 23, 2019. The Meteoritical Bulletin reports that the first recovered stone broke through a house, a 280 g piece struck a doghouse, and hundreds of stones totaling about 27 kg were recovered, including approximately 11 kg collected before rain reached the fall site (code 69696).
items.imageAlt: Broad face of the exact 4.97 g Aguas Zarcas CM2 specimen offered for sale
